title: Choosing speech use cases · Level 2
slo: Identify when speech recognition, speech synthesis, or both fit a workplace need.

exercises.question_text: Which media items can speech synthesis help create? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Synthesis can help create podcast drafts quickly.
Correct. Synthesis can create audiobook prototypes for rapid development.
Correct. Creators can use synthesis for video and presentation voiceovers.

options.error_type: Confuses media synthesis with meeting recognition
options.rationale: Action-item lists are written meeting documentation. Podcast drafts, audiobooks, and voiceovers are spoken media outputs.
options.better_fit: Use this when meeting conversations need follow-up lists and searchable documentation.

feedback.intrinsic: The media project would not gain the intended audio draft or voiceover.
feedback.instructional: Recognition supports meeting notes and action items. Synthesis creates spoken media.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Synthesis supports podcast drafts, audiobook prototypes, and video voiceovers.

exercises.question_text: What can speech synthesis adjust in a voice-agent response? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Synthesis can adjust tone to shape how a response sounds.
Correct. Synthesis can adjust pace in a spoken response.
Correct. Synthesis can use different speaking styles for more personalized interactions.

options.error_type: Confuses synthesis settings with recognition analysis
options.rationale: Call sentiment is analyzed from what a caller says. Tone, pace, and speaking style describe how the response is spoken.
options.better_fit: Use this when reviewing customer calls to identify sentiment and common issues.

feedback.intrinsic: The response might sound appropriate, but the caller’s sentiment would not be identified.
feedback.instructional: Synthesis shapes output voice qualities. Recognition can analyze spoken calls for sentiment.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Tone, pace, and speaking style all shape a synthesized response.

exercises.question_text: A service center can use speech recognition to create searchable call ___.

parts.text: A service center can use speech recognition to create searchable call

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The service center would not have the written result needed for later search and review.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Audio, alerts, and narration are spoken outputs or source material. Recognition creates searchable call records.

exercises.explanation: Recognition transcribes spoken calls into written records. Those records can be searched for compliance, training, and agent reference.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: It becomes unclear who is documenting and where the notes belong.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Start with the clinicians, then their dictated notes, then the electronic health records.

exercises.correct_answer: Clinical professionals dictate patient notes into electronic health records
exercises.explanation: The sentence follows the documentation flow: clinicians speak notes, and the notes enter electronic health records. This helps capture details during care.

exercises.question_text: A warehouse worker is carrying boxes and needs to set a reminder without using a screen. Which solution should the team choose?

options.text: A voice assistant that accepts a spoken reminder command
options.rationale: Correct. The worker needs hands-free spoken input to set a reminder while carrying boxes.

options.text: A tool that reads a document aloud
options.error_type: Confuses command input with spoken content output
options.rationale: Reading a document aloud gives spoken output. It does not capture the worker’s reminder command.
options.better_fit: Use this when someone needs to listen to written material instead of reading it.

feedback.intrinsic: The worker still could not set the reminder by speaking.
feedback.instructional: This need starts with a spoken command, so recognition is required.

options.text: A system that narrates a training lesson
options.error_type: Confuses hands-free control with learning narration
options.rationale: Narrated lessons provide educational audio. They do not accept a worker’s request to set a reminder.
options.better_fit: Use this for course content that needs spoken narration.

feedback.intrinsic: The reminder would not be created while the worker carries boxes.
feedback.instructional: Choose a voice assistant when the person must give a hands-free command.

options.text: A tool that creates a game character voice
options.error_type: Confuses workplace command use with media synthesis
options.rationale: A game character voice is media output. It does not support spoken workplace commands.
options.better_fit: Use this for games or interactive media that need character voices.

feedback.intrinsic: The worker’s reminder request would go unhandled.
feedback.instructional: The important need is recognizing the spoken reminder command, not creating media audio.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Recognition lets the assistant receive a spoken reminder request when screens are impractical.

exercises.question_text: During patient appointments, a clinic wants staff to capture details immediately and spend less time typing. Which choices should the clinic use? Select all that apply.

options.text: Dictate notes into electronic health records
options.rationale: Correct. Dictation enters spoken patient notes into electronic health records.
Correct. Clinical professionals can update treatment plans without interrupting care.
Correct. Speaking notes during care helps capture details immediately.

options.error_type: Confuses clinical documentation with media synthesis
options.rationale: Game character voices are media content. They do not document patient care or reduce appointment typing.
options.better_fit: Use this when producing voices for games or interactive experiences.

feedback.intrinsic: Staff would still need another way to capture patient details.
feedback.instructional: This clinic need is spoken documentation, which uses recognition rather than media synthesis.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These choices support spoken clinical documentation and reduce time spent typing.

exercises.question_text: Speech synthesis can read documents ___ for people who cannot read a screen.

parts.text: for people who cannot read a screen.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The person would not receive the document through an audible format.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: “Into text,” captions, and records describe written output. Synthesis reads written documents aloud.

exercises.explanation: Synthesis converts written documents into spoken audio. This provides an audio alternative when reading a screen is difficult or not possible.

exercises.question_text: Arrange the parts to form the correct statement.

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: The team could take on a complex flow before confirming the most valuable capability.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: The recommendation begins with one high-value capability and delays expansion until it is proven.

exercises.correct_answer: Start with one high-value speech capability then expand
exercises.explanation: Begin with the capability that addresses the most valuable need, then prove it works before adding a more complex voice flow. This keeps early work focused.

exercises.question_text: A commuter is driving and wants to consume company articles without reading a screen. Which solution should the company provide?

options.rationale: Correct. The commuter needs written articles converted into spoken audio while driving.
Articles are already written content, so transcription does not meet the need. The commuter needs audio output.
options.better_fit: Use transcription when spoken content needs to become written notes or records.

feedback.intrinsic: The commuter would still have to read rather than listen.
feedback.instructional: Synthesis reads written articles aloud; recognition transcribes spoken words into text.

options.error_type: Confuses content consumption with service recognition
options.rationale: Call routing helps send callers to the right department. It does not make written articles audible.
options.better_fit: Use this in customer service when callers state what they need.

feedback.intrinsic: The commuter would not be able to listen to the articles.
feedback.instructional: Choose synthesis when written content must be heard instead of read.

options.error_type: Confuses spoken output with recognition captions
options.rationale: Live captions turn spoken meetings into written words. The commuter instead needs written articles turned into audio.
options.better_fit: Use this to make a live spoken meeting accessible through written captions.

feedback.intrinsic: The articles would remain silent while the commuter drives.
feedback.instructional: Captions use recognition; reading articles aloud uses synthesis.

exercises.explanation: Correct. Synthesized audio lets the commuter consume written articles without looking at a screen.

exercises.question_text: Educational platforms can use speech synthesis to create narrated ___ without recording studios.

parts.text: Educational platforms can use speech synthesis to create narrated

feedback_for_incorrect.intrinsic: Learners would not receive the intended narrated course content.
feedback_for_incorrect.instructional: Call records, captions, and treatment plans are written results of recognition or documentation. Synthesis creates narrated lessons.

exercises.explanation: Synthesis creates spoken course content from written material, so lessons can be narrated without a recording studio. It can also support different learning preferences.

exercises.question_text: A driver says “call home,” and the vehicle must confirm the action aloud. Which design should the vehicle team choose?

options.text: Use speech recognition and speech synthesis together
options.rationale: Correct. Recognition captures “call home” as spoken input, and synthesis provides the audible confirmation.

options.error_type: Confuses two-way interaction with transcription alone
options.rationale: Call transcription can capture the driver’s words as text. It cannot provide the required spoken confirmation.
options.better_fit: Use this when a service center needs searchable written records of customer calls.

feedback.intrinsic: The driver could speak the command but would not hear confirmation.
feedback.instructional: A two-way interaction needs recognition for the command and synthesis for the reply.

options.error_type: Confuses vehicle interaction with learning synthesis
options.rationale: Lesson narration can speak educational content. It does not recognize the driver’s command or make a responsive confirmation.
options.better_fit: Use this when an educational platform needs narrated course material.

feedback.intrinsic: The vehicle would not respond appropriately to “call home.”
feedback.instructional: Narration is one-way audio. The driver needs both spoken input and spoken output.

options.rationale: Navigation alerts provide one-way spoken directions or updates. They do not capture a driver’s command before responding.
options.better_fit: Use this when the vehicle only needs to announce directions or status information.

feedback.intrinsic: The driver’s request would not be received as a command.
feedback.instructional: A confirmation after a spoken request requires recognition plus synthesis.

exercises.explanation: Correct. The vehicle needs recognition for the spoken command and synthesis for the audible confirmation.

exercises.question_text: A factory supervisor must give workers urgent equipment updates while they keep their eyes on machinery. Which features should the factory use? Select all that apply.

options.rationale: Correct. Spoken status announcements communicate operational information without requiring visual attention.
Correct. Synthesis can deliver urgent information when workers cannot safely look away.
Correct. Spoken updates help workers receive information while focused on machinery.

options.error_type: Confuses alert output with recognition transcription
options.rationale: Transcription creates written text from conversations. The supervisor needs urgent information announced aloud.
options.better_fit: Use this when spoken conversations need written records or captions.

feedback.intrinsic: Workers might not hear the urgent equipment update in time.
feedback.instructional: This need is spoken output for alerts, so use synthesis rather than transcription.

exercises.explanation: Correct. These spoken features deliver urgent information while workers keep visual attention on machinery.
